title: The Palace of a Thousand Logs
synopsis: Ten great logs for the new palace are missing from the timber yard.
A note with a small water drop says one mark has a new line.
goal: Find out where the palace logs went, and what the new palace costs.

notes: Played under the glass (InspectScene): the log whose mark has one pale, new cut is the one the note describes; its torn yard tag leads to the typed word. Take the new line away (Sora's rule: a stronger sound adds one line, ㄴ then ㄷ) and 다 was 나: good logs, for the palace gates.
The marks are words of the app (each spot's line): the logs in the picture have plain carved patches, no letters.

Measured 2026-11-06 on the grid sheet of timber_yard.webp (picture.measuredOn): the thick log end on the left, the thin bent log in the centre, the tall straight log on the right with its blank tag hanging just right of it; the game writes each mark on its log's carved patch; no two areas overlap.

clueInputs.note: Sora's Lesson Board: a stronger sound adds one line (ㄴ, then ㄷ).

learning.objective: 목재장 게시판과 Sora의 규칙(a stronger sound adds one line)을 읽고, 새로 한 획이 더해진 표시를 찾아 원래 표시가 뜻하던 곳(palace gates)을 쓴다.
expressions: One mark has a new line.

play.title: The New Line
story: Every log has a mark carved on its end.
A note with a small water drop is nailed to a post.
Duri, a carpenter's apprentice, shows you the yard board.
play.letterIntro: The yard board, and the note:
play.letter:
Yard board: each log has a mark carved on its end.
가: the best logs, for the great halls.
나: good logs, for the palace gates.
다: not for the palace. They may be sold.
The note: "One mark has a new line. Find it."
Sora's board: a stronger sound adds one line: ㄴ, then ㄷ.
play.question: Find the log with a new line. Before the new line, where was it going?
hints: Look for a mark with one pale, new cut.
Take the new line away. Which mark is left? Read the yard board.
play.successMessage: It was a 나 log, for the palace gates!
transition: Someone cut one new line on a palace log.
Now it looks like a log to sell.
"How many logs were changed?" asks Duri.
play.orderFeedback: Not that word. Take the new line away: which mark is left?

play.title: The Yard Book
story: In the yard office, the clerk opens his book.
A timber dealer, Mr. Pyo, bought logs here this morning.
"Only logs marked 다," the clerk says. "Logs that may be sold."
play.letterIntro: The yard book, and Mr. Pyo's paper:
play.letter:
Yard book, last night: 나 logs: ten. 다 logs: six.
Yard book, this morning: 나 logs: none. 다 logs: sixteen.
Mr. Pyo's paper: "I bought every 다 log in the yard."
play.question: How many palace logs got a new line? Put in the number.

play.successMessage: Ten palace logs became logs to sell!

"Why would anyone do that?" you ask.

play.title: The Palace's Story
story: Duri takes you to the new palace. It is only half done.
"Mr. Pyo says the new coin buys less every week," Duri says.
"He wants logs, not coins. But first, hear the palace's story."
play.letter:
"The palace burned in the war of 1592."
"After it burned, it lay in ruins for a long time."
"The ruins stood until 1865. Then the rebuilding began."
"A new coin came in 1866, after the work began. Prices went up."
"Last night, ten palace logs got a new line."
play.question: Put the palace's story in order, up to last night.
hints: Look for 'after', 'until' and 'then' in Duri's words.
The palace is not finished yet. Set aside what has not happened yet.
play.successMessage: That is the palace's story, up to last night!
transition: A palace costs wood, money and work. Not only wood.
Duri points to a cart by the gate.
"Mr. Pyo's cart! The ten logs are on it!"
play.orderFeedback: Read Duri's words again: what came after the work began?

learningGoal.title: Reading marks, numbers and a palace's story

objectives: Find the mark with a new line.
Put the palace's story in order.
intro: Winter, 1866. You are a guest of the Heungseon Daewongun in Hanyang.
He leads the rebuilding of Gyeongbokgung, the great palace.
It burned in the war of 1592, and lay in ruins for a long time.
Now great pine logs fill the timber yard.
But this morning, ten logs for the palace are missing.
play.caseSummary: Mr. Pyo, a timber dealer, had a new line cut on ten palace logs. So 나 became 다: logs that may be sold. Duri, a young carpenter, wrote the note. The real story: Gyeongbokgung burned in 1592. The Heungseon Daewongun rebuilt it from 1865, and it was finished in 1868. It cost the people dearly. People had to give money. A new coin made prices go up. Many were called to hard work.

notes: PART 10 (2026-11-06), Case 04. The Heungseon Daewongun is real; his words here are made up. Duri, Mr. Pyo, the clerk, the yard board, the marks and the missing logs are made up.

Ends on checked facts: the final talk closes on the real cost of the rebuilding (h4 forced gifts of money, h5 the new coin of 1866 and rising prices, h6 farmers called to work), and the ending states the real rebuilding (h2 begun in the fourth month of 1865, the Daewongun leading it; h3 finished in 1868, the King moved in). Act 1's turning point: the same water drop in 1592, 1795 and 1866.
